subject: Re: Pricing follow-up & stakeholder alignment (token volumes, budget)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing follow-up & stakeholder alignment (token volumes, budget)

Thanks again for the time today, Olivia — great conversation. Pulling together a short recap and the asks we discussed so we can keep momentum: 

Call recap (high level):
- Use case: in-app summarization + search re-ranking for support articles (mostly text, avg. prompt ~400 tokens).
- Expected traffic: pilot -> ~50M tokens/month, production -> ~200M tokens/month (total tokens incl. prompt + completion).
- Performance needs: 95th pct latency < 300ms for short completions; can tolerate occasional higher latency on long batching jobs.

Pricing / cost qualification (items we need confirmed):
1) Confirm target unit economics: you mentioned a target of ~$800 / 1M tokens as a target price to evaluate; is that still the right ballpark for evaluation?
2) Confirm budget range: pilot budget you said ~ $25k–$50k for the next quarter, production budget planning range $100k–$250k/month.
3) Token mix: estimated 70% completions vs 30% prompts; average completion size ~700 tokens (we used this to estimate monthly spend).

Stakeholder alignment (please confirm names/contact details):
- Economic buyer (product/ops): who owns the final go/no-go for procurement?
- Budget owner (procurement/finance): who signs off on the monthly commitment?
- Finance approver (CFO / FP&A): is there a standardized procurement process or PO flow we should expect?

Next steps (what Redwood will do):
- Share a draft mutual action plan + token cost estimates for pilot and scaled scenarios (attached).
- Aditya and Rishi to put together a pricing model scoped to the 50M / 200M token scenarios and highlight where batching/quantization changes unit pricing.

Can you confirm the 3 items above (target $/1M, budget range, and stakeholder names) and we will follow up with a short MAP and a proposed contract path?

Attachments: Acme-MAP-20260610.xlsx (draft MAP), acme-token-estimates.csv (estimates)

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
https://redwood.com

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-ai.com>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@acme-ai.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up & stakeholder alignment (token volumes, budget)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and for sending the draft materials. Answers inline below.

Pricing / cost qualification:
- Target unit economics: yes, $800 / 1M tokens is the right target for our evaluation. If we can get below $700 / 1M at scale that would make procurement much easier.
- Budget range: pilot (Q3) – $30k (one-off pilot spend), production (Q4 planning) – $120k–$220k/month depending on model and performance.
- Token mix: those estimates look right (we'll attach a quick internal usage export later this week).

Stakeholders:
- Economic buyer: Daniel Park, VP Product (cc'd) — will own final go/no-go.
- Budget owner: Sana Patel, Head of Procurement (cc'd) — signs monthly commitments and POs.
- Finance approver: our FP&A/CFO review is coordinated through finance@acme-ai.com — typically one week for approvals on standard SaaS agreements; larger commitments (>$200k/month) go to CFO for review.

Next steps for us:
- I'll share the internal token export by EOD Thu.
- Please send the MAP + pricing scenarios and we can schedule a 30-min review with Daniel and Sana next week (Fri preferred).

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of AI Integrations | Acme AI
olivia.chen@acme-ai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-ai.com>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@acme-ai.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up & stakeholder alignment (token volumes, budget)

Perfect — thanks for confirming, Olivia. Looping Daniel and Sana on this thread so we can pick a time for a short pricing walkthrough.

Aditya / Rishi — heads up on CTAs for the review with Daniel/Sana next week (Fri).
- Action: please prepare 3 pricing scenarios (Pilot: 50M tokens, Production low: 100M tokens, Production high: 200M tokens) with line items: unit $/1M tokens, estimated monthly cost, options for Reserved/Dedicated pricing, and notes on where batching/quantization impacts pricing.
- Target to share slides + numbers by Thu EOD so Olivia can distribute internally.

Olivia / Daniel / Sana — can you confirm Fri 18 Jun 11:00am PT / 2:00pm ET works for a 30-min call? If not, propose an alternate window. We'll aim to keep the call focused on numbers and the MAP timeline so procurement can start the PO process if everything looks good.

—
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up & stakeholder alignment (token volumes, budget)

Thanks Marissa — noted. I'll take lead on the pricing model and Rishi can add detailed notes on batching/quant impacts. Quick clarifications before we finalize numbers:
- For the $800 / 1M target, are we assuming hosted (shared) API pricing or a Dedicated reserved capacity quote? It will materially change the unit math — I'll prepare both.
- Any preference on showing blended $/1M (after projected batching gains) vs. raw per-token rate? I recommend showing both so procurement sees the upside with workload optimizations.

I'll have a slide deck with three scenarios (Pilot / Prod low / Prod high) and a one-page appendix on assumptions by Thu EOD.

—
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
